title: Church Planting Readiness
subtitle: An honest count of the cost before you plant, of your calling, your family, your finances, and your capacity to live in the unknown.
intro:
This is not a green light and it is not a recruiting pitch. It is a quiet, sober count of the cost, the kind Jesus told the would-be builder to make before he laid a foundation he could not finish. Church planting is some of the most joyful and most brutal work in the kingdom. It breaks people who were gifted but not ready, and it breaks marriages that were never truly agreed.

Answer about your life as it actually is, not as you hope it will be once you are out there. No one reads this but you and God, and the people you will ask to read it with you. The result is a mirror, not a verdict and not a sending. It only shows you where you are strong and where you are not yet ready, so you can pray, prepare, and bring it to the people who would send you.

questions.text: I have a clear, tested sense of calling to plant, confirmed by others and not only felt by me in a moment of zeal.
My spouse is fully and genuinely with me in this, not merely going along to keep the peace.
My family understands what this will cost them in time, money, and stability, and they have counted it with open eyes.
I can keep going when the work is discouraging and the results are thin for a long time.
There is real financial runway, savings or support, so that a hard first year would not sink us.
I have actual sending support, a church or network that has committed to back, coach, and hold me accountable.
I genuinely love people who are far from God, and I share my faith naturally with those who do not believe.
I can live with ambiguity, with no set schedule and no clear map, without losing my footing.
I have a track record of starting something hard and seeing it through, not just dreaming about it.
My marriage is strong enough to absorb stress, loneliness, and disappointment without fracturing.
I am emotionally resilient, and I do not crumble or grow bitter when people leave or criticize me.
I am doing this for the kingdom and for lost people, not to prove something or to escape a situation I am in.
I can build a team and draw others into a vision, because a plant is never carried by one person.
My walk with God is deep enough to sustain me when the work, the platform, and the encouragement all run dry.
I have honestly faced my weaknesses and have people who will tell me hard truths and help me stay accountable.

bands.label: Not now, and rushing would cost you dearly
bands.body:
The honest reading is that the pieces are not in place, and to push forward now would be to build a foundation you cannot finish. This is not a word against your gifting or your love for God. It is the very thing Jesus told the builder to do before he started, and it is mercy, not discouragement.

Look at where the lowest answers fell, because that is where the warning is loudest. A spouse who is not truly with you. No financial runway. No sending support. A thin record of finishing hard things. A walk with God that is running on the work itself rather than feeding it. Plant in this condition and you will not only risk the plant. You will risk your marriage, your children, and your own soul.

Do not hear no as never. Hear it as not now, and let it send you to prepare. Get your family genuinely aligned, not merely compliant. Build the runway. Get under a sending body that will form you. Deepen the walk with God that has to outlast every result.

The call may be real. The readiness is not yet. Honor both by waiting.

bands.label: The desire is real, but the foundation is thin
bands.body:
There is something genuine here, a real desire and some real gifting, and it would be wrong to dismiss it. But the honest reading is that the foundation underneath the desire is thinner than the work requires, and church planting is unforgiving of thin foundations.

The danger at this stage is letting zeal outrun preparation. Zeal feels like calling, and in the heat of it the gaps are easy to ignore. But the gaps do not disappear when you launch. They get exposed, usually in the loneliest, hardest stretch, when there is no margin left to fix them.

Look hard at your lowest answers and treat them as the real agenda for the next season. If it is your family, do not move until they are truly with you, freely and with open eyes. If it is finances or sending support, build those before you build anything else. If it is resilience or your own walk with God, those are formed over time and not in a launch.

The desire is a good beginning. Let it become readiness before it becomes a plant.

bands.label: Much is in place, but test the weak seams
bands.body:
The honest reading is that much of what church planting demands is genuinely present in you and your situation. There is calling, some real support, a measure of resilience, and a love for lost people. That is a serious and hopeful thing. It is also not the same as being ready, and the difference is in the seams.

Do not let the strong overall picture blind you to the one or two answers that came back lower. Those are not noise. Under the pressure of a plant, the weakest seam is the one that tears, and it usually tears at the worst possible time. A marriage that is strong but stretched. Support that exists but is not fully committed. A walk with God that is real but thinner than the work will require.

This is the moment to strengthen the weak seams while you still have time and calm to do it. Get your spouse and family to genuine, eyes-open agreement. Nail down the sending support and the financial runway in writing, not in hope. Deepen the rhythms that feed your soul.

You are close. Close is exactly when honesty about the gaps matters most.

bands.label: The call and the capacity line up, so take the next concrete step
bands.body:
By your own honest reckoning, the calling and the capacity line up. The sense of call is tested, your family is genuinely with you, the runway and the sending support are real, you love lost people, and your walk with God runs deeper than the work. That is a gift, and it should make you both grateful and sober, because everything that is strong now will still be tested hard.

But hear this plainly. A strong reading on a self-examination is not a sending. It cannot see your marriage under real strain or your soul on the empty days, and it certainly cannot commission you. The decision to plant belongs with a sending church or network that knows you, has assessed you, and is willing to stand behind you and over you.

So do not let this confidence settle the matter in your own mind. Take it to the people who would send you, and ask them to test it hard, including the corners you suspect are softer than they look. Let your spouse speak freely and without pressure. Then take the next concrete step, an assessment, a residency, a conversation with a sending body, rather than a leap.

The call and the capacity line up. Now let the church confirm it and walk it with you.

closing: This is a mirror for honest discernment before God and your family, not a sending. A church or network that knows you confirms and commissions a planter, never a web tool and never a person alone in front of a screen.
